summary: Andrej Karpathy presents a systematic recipe for training neural networks, emphasizing that training is a leaky abstraction that fails silently. He advises a step-by-step process from thoroughly inspecting the data, setting up a reliable training/evaluation skeleton, overfitting a small model, then regularizing and tuning. The post stresses patience, attention to detail, and avoiding unverified complexity.

claims.text: Neural networks are not off-the-shelf technology once you deviate slightly from standard problems like ImageNet classification.
claims.evidence_quote: They are not “off-the-shelf” technology the second you deviate slightly from training an ImageNet classifier.

claims.text: A fast and furious approach to training neural networks does not work and leads to suffering.
claims.evidence_quote: a “fast and furious” approach to training neural networks does not work and only leads to suffering.

claims.text: Patience and attention to detail are the qualities that correlate most strongly with success in deep learning.
claims.evidence_quote: The qualities that in my experience correlate most strongly to success in deep learning are patience and attention to detail.

claims.text: The first step in training a neural network is to thoroughly inspect your data before touching any neural network code.
claims.evidence_quote: The first step to training a neural net is to not touch any neural net code at all and instead begin by thoroughly inspecting your data.

claims.text: Always use a fixed random seed to guarantee reproducibility.
claims.evidence_quote: Always use a fixed random seed to guarantee that when you run the code twice you will get the same outcome.

claims.text: Verify that the loss starts at the correct value at initialization, such as -log(1/n_classes) for a softmax.
claims.evidence_quote: If you initialize your final layer correctly you should measure `-log(1/n_classes)` on a softmax at initialization.

claims.text: Overfitting a single batch of only a few examples can verify that the model learns and predictions align with labels.
claims.evidence_quote: Overfit a single batch of only a few examples (e.g. as little as two).

claims.text: When choosing an architecture, resist creativity and copy the simplest architecture from the most related paper.
Adam is much more forgiving to hyperparameters, including a bad learning rate.
claims.evidence_quote: In my experience Adam is much more forgiving to hyperparameters, including a bad learning rate.

claims.text: Use Adam with a learning rate of 3e-4 for early baselines.
claims.evidence_quote: I like to use Adam with a learning rate of [3e-4]

claims.text: Do not trust learning rate decay defaults from reused code, as they can drive the learning rate to zero too early.
claims.evidence_quote: do not trust learning rate decay defaults

claims.text: Adding more real training data is the best and preferred way to regularize a model.
claims.evidence_quote: the by far best and preferred way to regularize a model in any practical setting is to add more real training data.

claims.text: Use random search instead of grid search for hyperparameter tuning.
claims.evidence_quote: it is best to use random search instead

claims.text: Model ensembles are a pretty much guaranteed way to gain 2% accuracy on anything.
claims.evidence_quote: Model ensembles are a pretty much guaranteed way to gain 2% of accuracy on anything.

claims.text: A model accidentally left training over a winter break became state of the art.
claims.evidence_quote: One time I accidentally left a model training during the winter break and when I got back in January it was SOTA (“state of the art”).
